Fourth release candidate for open[flow] 0.1.0, focused on the mix[flow] four-deck mixer: what a deck keeps, how it switches sources, and where its timing is set.

## Changes since RC3

- A deck now opens on the original track and reaches its stems when a stem clip asks for them. Switching between the two no longer pauses either: the mode is a gain ramp and the incoming source takes the audible position, so the deck plays on through the swap.
- Loading a track keeps the channel as the desk was set — fader, trim, EQ, filter, both sends, crossfader assignment, headphone cue, and Sync where the new track has a grid. Only stem levels reset.
- Launch timing, marker quantize and quick loop length are the rig's, set in the header and shared by every deck; the quick loop defaults to two bars. The master strip's old launch toggle wrote a value nothing read and is gone.
- In and Out are the running loop's boundaries when pressed inside one, snapped to the marker division, which retires the boundary nudges. Halve/double and the loop move sit on the deck beside the quick loop.
- The mix and the headphone cue each go to a stereo pair chosen by name rather than a fixed 1/2 and 3/4. An interface too narrow for a saved pair falls back to the front pair with the cue dropped rather than folded into the room.
- Every deck meters its own left and right, and the deck fader is a slot and a cap with a ruled scale, drawn on the strip rather than inside a well.

## Known issue: a multi-output interface offers one stereo pair

Since mid-2026 the browser engine asks macOS for a device's preferred *speaker layout* instead of its channel count, and most interfaces publish a stereo layout however many outputs they have. Wrap the interface in an Aggregate Device in Audio MIDI Setup and choose that as the output; the aggregate publishes no layout, so every channel appears. Troubleshooting in the wiki carries the steps. The routing itself is unaffected and needs no change when the count is reported correctly.

## Downloads

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `mix-flow-0.1.0-rc.4-arm64.dmg` | mix[flow]: local stem separation, track preparation and four-deck playback. |
| `set-flow-0.1.0-rc.4-arm64.dmg` | set[flow]: the Ableton Live session manager. |
| `visual-flow-0.1.0-rc.4-arm64.dmg` | visual[flow]: the visual performance app. |
| `SessionBridge-0.1.0-rc.4.zip` | Max for Live bridge for set[flow] and visual[flow]. Keep its three device files together. |

Apple silicon only. The release workflow requires signing, notarization, Gatekeeper and stapled-ticket checks before attaching installers. mix[flow] runs independently of Live and the bridge. Its first separation downloads the managed Python environment, dependencies and model weights. Automatic updates remain disabled; install this version explicitly.

## Before the final release

Test the signed installer on a clean Mac: import, first-run engine setup, cancellation and retry, separation, four-deck playback, and persistence after quitting and reopening. Exercise the source swap, Cue, quick and manual loops, Slip, beat jumps and synchronization with real tracks — the timing and source changes in this candidate affect where a deck lands. Verify the mix and cue pairs on a multichannel interface, and headphone monitoring against the room.

The mixer changes were measured against the running app and are covered by engine tests. That pass found a fault the tests could not: a deck switched to stems it had never played sat silent at zero, because every engine test reaches stems through a fixture that enables them first. Neither replaces clean-machine or hardware testing, and Live/device behavior is unverified by this release preparation.

For installation details, see [Installing](https://github.com/ryangavin/better-session-view/wiki/Installing). Include the release version, macOS version, audio hardware and reproduction steps when reporting a problem.
